title: Finite scalar restriction preserves constructible complexes and bounds
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $a:A\to A'$ a homomorphism of finite commutative rings, and $a_X:A_X\to A'_X$ the induced morphism of constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] on its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] is exact on module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and thus induces a termwise functor $D(a_X):D(A'_X)\to D(A_X)$ on unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It sends each constructible sheaf of $A'_X$-modules to a constructible sheaf of $A_X$-modules [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf], using the same stratification and trivializing covers. For every $L\in D(A'_X)$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, $H^q(D(a_X)L)\cong\operatorname{Res}_{a_X}H^q(L)$. In particular it preserves bounded constructibility and preserves and reflects vanishing of cohomology in each degree. Surjectivity of $a$ is not assumed.

source.place: Second paragraph, last sentence: regard the outer finite-coefficient terms as R_n-modules by scalar restriction.
